thread_b.role: concurrent IPv6 route lookup probe rate-limit (reader+updater)

emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(last_probe), time_after check, write(last_probe = jiffies)]) -- the rate-limit read-check-update must be one indivisible region so only one CPU wins per interval
emergent_bug.violating_event: e@rt6_probe:663 = WRITE(last_probe = jiffies) by the peer CPU interleaving INSIDE the other CPU's read-check-update region
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: rt6_probe holds only rcu_read_lock_bh (does not serialize two CPUs on this nexthop) -> no serialize over the [read..write] region; both CPUs read the same stale last_probe, both pass time_after, both update and queue a deferred probe
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic(REGION = read -> check -> update), broken by an interleaving write inside the region -> atomicity violation (manifests as the KCSAN data race plus duplicate deferred rt6_probe works)

fix_maps_to: patch samples last_probe = READ_ONCE(...) and replaces the conditional plain store with cmpxchg(&fib6_nh->last_probe, last_probe, jiffies) -> makes the read-check-update an atomic compare-and-swap so only one CPU commits -> establishes atomic(region). (Separately it also fixes the last_probe == 0 init, a 32-bit single-thread logic issue, not the race.)
recall_risk_notes: Self-race: static must model the same rt6_probe on two CPUs against the same shared fib6_nh. Region-boundary inference is needed: the assume must span [read@657 .. write@663]; a single-point assume would degrade to a plain data_race (still a recall, but the cmpxchg fix confirms the region is the true ρ). The benign-ish outcome (duplicate probe work) is a mild dismissal risk. Object identity via find_match(nh) -> rt6_probe(fib6_nh) is clean.
